differences.what: massing: the draft's generic block is now the plate's house: a narrow red brick front two storeys over a stone basement under a steep slated hip with a street dormer, its long north flank running back past a round tower to steep-gabled half-storey ranges and a two-storey garage; the two tall stacks, the tower, the dormer and the front's corners lie within about 15-25 px of the plate (16 px RMS on the fitted points)

the broad bow across the front's north part, which the plate shows as the wall and eave sweeping round from the north corner: built as a K08 bow, 6.0 m on its chord and 1.0 m out, where the 1911 sheet draws the front swelling 0.8 m forward

the front's north corner: the plate sweeps the eave round it in a curve and the sheet cuts it back about 0.85 by 1.2 m; built square (K01 cuts a canted corner only under a mansard and rounds one only in a stone front)
the bow is carried up to the eave in the plate, the main cornice running round it; built stopping under the cornice's bed with a nearly flat cap (K08 stops a bay below the bed moulding)
the round tower: the plate takes it about 2 m higher than built, with a broader, more solid top; the build's low slated cone is the kit's
the north flank's two-storey bays with flat tops (balconies over them) across the rear ranges, and the rear range's canted north bay the sheet draws: not built, the ranges' north walls are flat
the steep gables over the rear ranges: the plate draws three or more, stepped and finialled at their peaks; built as two plain slated gables
the street dormer: the plate's is broad, three lights under its gable; built with one sash at the K01 contract's widest
the entrance at the stoop's head: the plate shows an arched opening beside the south neighbour; built as K07's square-headed panelled door
stone belts and dressings: the plate shows pale stone courses and window dressings across the brick; built with plain stone lintels only
windows: their count and places along the front and the flank are the kit's, not read (the plate is too coarse and the trees hide the lower storey)
colour: the brick's red, the stone's tone and the slate are read from later photographs and the trade's materials; the plate is monochrome

the south neighbour (1923, the mansard at the plate's right edge), the street trees, the lamp post and the iron fence's pattern: not part of this record (the fence is K11's scroll band, its pattern unreadable)

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236). A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
